tasks.title: Autonomous loop: pre-flight auth smoke, mechanical cycle-outcome ledger and fast-fail paging
tasks.summary: Delivered: the loop trigger now runs a bounded one-turn pre-flight smoke of the headless runtime before launching and, on failure, launches nothing, files an alert task and pages; the service manager records every launched cycle's outcome mechanically; the watchdog pages when three consecutive recorded cycles end within seconds. Root cause of the nine-day outage recorded: a stale headless CLI on the service path could not refresh its expired token while interactive use could. Tests 23/23 and 51/51; verified live with a real smoke, a simulated expired-token runtime, and a replay of the real outage.
tasks.next_action: Observe the 16:20 and 20:20 UTC trigger slots after the token expiry: a failed refresh must now page and file a task instead of silently launching dead cycles. Separate finding filed: mission write routes accept unauthenticated local callers.

tasks.title: Mission store: authenticate every write route (create, edit, tape, decision ruling) — no unauthenticated local caller
tasks.summary: Delivered: every mission-store write (create, edit, event-tape append, decision ruling) now requires a real credential; anonymous, wrong-token and identity-header-only callers are refused and nothing is written; observers are refused with an audit row; a sandboxed engineering agent may edit only work it currently holds, closing a reword-then-claim escalation; rulings are board-only; rows and audit name the authenticated actor. New tests 27/27 (26 failed before the fix), suite 339, real-money bolt 10/10, paper gate confirmed. An independent adversarial verification against the running service confirmed the refusals and that nothing was written; the observer refusal is proven in the harness only. Every existing writer already sent credentials, so nothing broke.
tasks.next_action: Filed for follow-up: the console's server-side proxy still grants operator authority to anonymous callers (high); the lease-sweep route has no auth (low); the loop's failure path marks a blocked mission with an invalid column (medium). Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item.

tasks.title: Console: require a verified operator session for every mission-store write made through the console, and name the human in the audit trail
tasks.summary: Delivered: every write made through the console to the mission store now requires a verified operator session — an HttpOnly signed cookie from a one-time operator sign-in, or a verified edge-login identity; anonymous, spoofed-identity, forged-cookie and forged-edge-token writes are refused at the console before the store is contacted, and a cross-site browser context is refused even with a session. Reads are unchanged. The audit trail now names the signed-in person instead of a generic operator. New tests 37 (all failed before the fix), console suite 304, real-money bolt 10/10, paper gate confirmed. An independent adversarial verification against the running console (private network and edge included) confirmed every refusal and the attribution; the positive edge-login path is proven in the harness only. Two of its low findings (sign-in lockout, key-set refresh flooding) were fixed in-cycle; the rest filed.
tasks.next_action: Filed for follow-up: a console rewrite forwards every method to the trading backend without a gate (high); reads through the console proxy still carry operator authority (low); session hardening — revocation on sign-out, stricter origin check (low). Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: a blocked cycle outcome must be recorded on the mission board (the store refused the marker the loop sent)
tasks.summary: Delivered: a blocked cycle outcome now lands on the mission board. The loop's finish step marks the held mission with the store's supported paused flag, keeps the reason comment, and hands the lease back, so the item shows as paused, is skipped by the work queue and the watchdog digest names it instead of paging. The test harness's fake store now enforces the real column contract and pagination (it previously accepted a value the real store rejects), and store-level tests pin the contract. Proven on a scratch copy of the real store (old path refused with an error and wedged; new path lands), then independently verified: holds with caveats. Two follow-ups fixed in-cycle (paged revision lookup, fixture label); negative-path hardening filed.
tasks.next_action: Next cycle: reconcile and pick the highest in-boundary item — candidates: loop finish negative-path hardening (re-claim on a reaped lease, idempotent comment, reason on the row), console session hardening, reads through the console proxy carrying operator authority.

tasks.title: Autonomous loop: the watchdog must re-open its own archived page for a build workspace that reappears, instead of failing to file a duplicate every run
tasks.summary: In progress: the mission store's list view hides archived records and offers no way to include them, so the loop watchdog cannot see an archived page it retired earlier; when a build workspace reappears at that path it tries to file the same identifier again, the store rejects the duplicate, and the watchdog pages 'auto-file failed' on every run without ever re-opening the record. Fix in lock-step: the store's list view gains an opt-in switch to include archived records (default unchanged), and the watchdog uses it to look up its own retired pages, re-opening them under the same identifier. Same gap closed for the other two self-filed deterministic identifiers.
